questions.question: 'पल्लव' नामक काव्य संग्रह के रचयिता कौन हैं?

options.explanation: जयशंकर प्रसाद छायावादी कवि नहीं थे, बल्कि उनके प्रमुख काव्य संग्रह 'कामायनी' हैं।
निराला जी का प्रमुख काव्य संग्रह 'परिमल' है, 'पल्लव' नहीं।
सुमित्रानंदन पंत द्वारा रचित 'पल्लव' एक प्रसिद्ध काव्य संग्रह है।
महादेवी वर्मा का प्रमुख काव्य संग्रह 'नीरजा' है, 'पल्लव' नहीं।

questions.explanation: 'पल्लव' सुमित्रानंदन पंत का एक अत्यंत प्रसिद्ध काव्य संग्रह है, जिसे छायावाद का घोषणापत्र (मेनिफेस्टो) भी कहा जाता है।
questions.hint: यह काव्य संग्रह छायावादी कवि द्वारा रचित है।
questions.subject: dsssb-hindi

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी विशेषता छायावाद की प्रमुख विशेषता नहीं है?

options.explanation: वैयक्तिकता का प्राधान्य छायावाद की प्रमुख विशेषता है।
प्रकृति का मानवीकरण भी छायावाद की प्रमुख विशेषता है।

options.text: स्थूल के प्रति सूक्ष्म का विद्रोह
options.explanation: स्थूल के प्रति सूक्ष्म का विद्रोह छायावाद की प्रमुख विशेषता है।

options.text: शोषक वर्ग के प्रति घृणा और शोषित वर्ग के प्रति सहानुभूति
options.explanation: यह विशेषता प्रगतिवाद की है, न कि छायावाद की।

questions.explanation: शोषक वर्ग के प्रति घृणा और शोषित वर्ग के प्रति सहानुभूति मुख्य रूप से प्रगतिवाद की विशेषता है, जबकि अन्य विकल्प छायावाद की प्रमुख विशेषताएँ हैं।
questions.hint: छायावाद में व्यक्तिगत भावनाओं और प्रकृति के चित्रण पर अधिक जोर दिया जाता है।
questions.subject: dsssb-hindi

questions.question: जयशंकर प्रसाद के महाकाव्य 'कामायनी' में कुल कितने सर्ग हैं?

options.explanation: 12 सर्ग 'कामायनी' में नहीं हैं।
'कामायनी' में कुल 15 सर्ग हैं।
17 सर्ग 'कामायनी' में नहीं हैं।
20 सर्ग 'कामायनी' में नहीं हैं।

questions.explanation: जयशंकर प्रसाद द्वारा रचित महाकाव्य 'कामायनी' में कुल 15 सर्ग हैं, जो क्रमशः चिंता, आशा, श्रद्धा, काम, वासना, लज्जा, कर्म, ईर्ष्या, इड़ा, स्वप्न, संघर्ष, निर्वेद, दर्शन, रहस्य और आनंद हैं।
questions.hint: यह महाकाव्य छायावादी कवि द्वारा रचित है।

questions.question: ओ मेरे आदर्शवादी मन! ओ मेरे सिद्धांतवादी मन! अब तक क्या किया? जीवन क्या जिया? ये पंक्तियाँ किस कवि की हैं?

options.explanation: पंत जी की रचनाओं में ऐसी व्यंग्यात्मक पंक्तियाँ नहीं मिलतीं।
प्रसाद जी की रचनाओं में ऐसी व्यंग्यात्मक पंक्तियाँ नहीं मिलतीं।
ये पंक्तियाँ निराला जी की कविता 'कुकुरमुत्ता' से हैं।
महादेवी वर्मा की रचनाओं में ऐसी व्यंग्यात्मक पंक्तियाँ नहीं मिलतीं।

questions.explanation: ये पंक्तियाँ सूर्यकांत त्रिपाठी 'निराला' की प्रसिद्ध व्यंग्यात्मक कविता 'कुकुरमुत्ता' से उद्धृत हैं, जिसमें उन्होंने तत्कालीन सामाजिक विसंगतियों और आदर्शों के खोखलेपन पर व्यंग्य किया है।
questions.hint: यह कवि छायावादी दौर के प्रमुख कवियों में से एक हैं।

questions.question: छायावाद और प्रगतिवाद दोनों काव्य धाराओं का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाले कवि कौन हैं?

options.explanation: प्रसाद जी मुख्य रूप से छायावादी कवि थे, प्रगतिवादी नहीं।
पंत जी ने दोनों काव्य धाराओं में योगदान दिया।
महादेवी वर्मा मुख्य रूप से छायावादी कवयित्री थीं।
रामकुमार वर्मा का संबंध अन्य साहित्यिक आंदोलनों से था।

questions.explanation: सुमित्रानंदन पंत ने जहाँ 'पल्लव', 'गुंजन' जैसी रचनाओं से छायावाद का प्रतिनिधित्व किया, वहीं 'युगांत', 'युगवाणी', 'ग्राम्या' जैसी रचनाओं में प्रगतिवादी चेतना को अभिव्यक्त किया।
questions.hint: यह कवि दोनों काव्य धाराओं में समान रूप से सक्रिय रहे।

questions.question: प्रगतिवाद केवल छायावाद का विकसित रूप नहीं है, बल्कि वह उसकी प्रतिक्रिया भी है। यह कथन किस आलोचक का है?

options.explanation: आचार्य शुक्ल ने प्रगतिवाद को छायावाद का विकसित रूप नहीं माना।
डॉ. नगेंद्र ने ऐसा कथन नहीं किया।
रामविलास शर्मा ने यह कथन व्यक्त किया।
हजारी प्रसाद द्विवेदी ने ऐसा कथन नहीं किया।

questions.explanation: रामविलास शर्मा ने प्रगतिवाद को केवल छायावाद का विकसित रूप नहीं, बल्कि उसकी प्रतिक्रिया के रूप में देखा।
questions.hint: यह आलोचक हिंदी साहित्य के इतिहास में प्रमुख स्थान रखते हैं।

questions.question: 'पल्लव' नामक काव्य-संग्रह के रचयिता कौन हैं?

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन छायावाद के चार स्तंभों (बृहत्त्रयी) में शामिल नहीं है?

options.explanation: जयशंकर प्रसाद छायावाद के चार स्तंभों में शामिल हैं।
सुमित्रानंदन पंत छायावाद के चार स्तंभों में शामिल हैं।
महादेवी वर्मा छायावाद के चार स्तंभों में शामिल हैं।
रामकुमार वर्मा छायावाद के चार स्तंभों में शामिल नहीं हैं।

questions.explanation: छायावाद के चार स्तंभ जयशंकर प्रसाद, सुमित्रानंदन पंत, सूर्यकांत त्रिपाठी 'निराला' और महादेवी वर्मा हैं। रामकुमार वर्मा एक प्रमुख छायावादी कवि हैं, परंतु वे 'चार स्तंभों' में नहीं गिने जाते।

questions.question: प्रगतिवाद का मूल स्वर क्या है?

options.explanation: यह छायावाद की विशेषता है, प्रगतिवाद की नहीं।
यह रहस्यवाद की विशेषता है, प्रगतिवाद की नहीं।
प्रगतिवाद का मूल स्वर सामाजिक यथार्थ और शोषक-शोषित संघर्ष है।
यह राष्ट्रीय काव्यधारा की विशेषता है, प्रगतिवाद की नहीं।

questions.explanation: प्रगतिवाद मार्क्सवादी विचारधारा से प्रभावित काव्यधारा है, जिसका मूल स्वर सामाजिक यथार्थ, वर्ग-संघर्ष, पूंजीवाद का विरोध और शोषितों के प्रति सहानुभूति है।

options.text: Expanding assured irrigation coverage ('Per Drop More Crop').

options.text: Promoting organic farming practices across the country.
options.explanation: Organic farming is promoted under other schemes, not PMKSY.

questions.explanation: The primary objective of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY) is to expand the cultivated area under assured irrigation, improve water use efficiency ('Per Drop More Crop'), and enhance the adoption of precision irrigation technologies.

questions.question: Which state in India is the largest producer of Mica?

options.explanation: Karnataka is not a major producer of mica.
Chhattisgarh has mica deposits but is not the largest producer.
Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of mica in India.
Odisha has mica deposits but is not the largest producer.

questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh is the leading producer of Mica in India, particularly known for its high-quality ruby mica. Jharkhand and Rajasthan also have significant deposits, but Andhra Pradesh holds the top position.
questions.hint: Andhra Pradesh is known for its mineral wealth, including mica.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the impact of the Green Revolution in India: I. It led to an increase in regional disparities in agricultural development. II. It primarily focused on increasing the yield of coarse grains. III. It contributed to the problem of groundwater depletion in some regions. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.explanation: Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II is incorrect.
Both statements I and III are correct.
Statement II is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: The Green Revolution primarily benefited states with better irrigation facilities like Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh, leading to increased regional disparities. Statement III is correct: The intensive use of irrigation, particularly groundwater, for high-yielding varieties led to significant groundwater depletion in many regions. Statement II is incorrect: The Green Revolution primarily focused on increasing the yield of wheat and rice, not coarse grains.
questions.hint: The Green Revolution had mixed impacts, including regional disparities and environmental issues.
questions.subject: dsssb-gk

questions.question: Black soil (Regur soil) is most suitable for the cultivation of which of the following crops?

options.explanation: Jute is grown in alluvial soil, not black soil.
Black soil is highly suitable for cotton cultivation.
Tea is grown in hilly regions with acidic soil.
Groundnut is grown in sandy loam soil.

questions.explanation: Black soil, also known as Regur soil, is highly retentive of moisture and rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, making it ideal for cotton cultivation. It is predominantly found in the Deccan Trap region.
questions.hint: Black soil is known for its fertility and moisture retention, ideal for specific crops.
questions.subject: dsssb-gk

questions.question: 'Operation Flood' is associated with which of the following?

options.explanation: Operation Flood is not related to flood control.
Increasing fish production is not the focus of Operation Flood.
Operation Flood is known as the 'White Revolution' for dairy development.
Sericulture is the practice of silk farming, unrelated to Operation Flood.

questions.explanation: Operation Flood, launched in 1970, was a landmark program by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) that transformed India into the world's largest milk producer. It is commonly known as the 'White Revolution'.
questions.hint: Operation Flood is related to dairy development and milk production.
questions.subject: dsssb-gk

questions.question: Which of the following types of farming is characterized by the cultivation of high-value crops like fruits, vegetables, and flowers, often with intensive use of capital and labor, and usually located near urban centers?

options.explanation: Shifting cultivation involves clearing and burning forest areas for temporary agriculture.
Extensive farming involves large land areas with low labor and capital input.
Plantation agriculture involves large-scale monoculture of crops like tea or coffee.
Truck farming involves high-value crops and is located near urban centers.

questions.explanation: Truck farming is a form of commercial gardening and fruit farming where farmers specialize in growing vegetables, fruits, and flowers, primarily for sale in distant urban markets. The term 'truck' refers to the transport of these products to market. It is capital and labor-intensive.
questions.hint: This type of farming involves high-value crops and is located near urban centers.

questions.question: Which state in India is the largest producer of Coffee?

options.explanation: Kerala is a significant producer but not the largest.
Tamil Nadu is a significant producer but not the largest.
Karnataka is the largest producer of coffee in India.
Andhra Pradesh is not a major producer of coffee.

questions.explanation: Karnataka is the largest producer of coffee in India, accounting for over 70% of the country's total coffee production. The Kodagu, Chikmagalur, and Hassan districts are major coffee-growing regions.
questions.hint: Karnataka is known for its coffee plantations.
questions.subject: dsssb-gk

questions.question: What does the term 'Agro-climatic Zones' primarily refer to in the context of Indian agriculture?

options.text: Regions identified for specific forest conservation efforts.
options.explanation: Agro-climatic zones are not primarily for forest conservation.

options.text: Areas designated for the development of agro-based industries.
options.explanation: Agro-climatic zones are not designated for agro-based industries.

options.text: Regions characterized by similar climate, soil, and water resources, suitable for specific crops.
options.explanation: This is the primary definition of agro-climatic zones.

options.text: Zones where only organic farming is permitted by government regulations.
options.explanation: Agro-climatic zones are not restricted to organic farming.

questions.explanation: Agro-climatic zones are geographic regions delineated based on common characteristics such as climate (temperature, rainfall, humidity), soil type, and water availability, which influence the suitability of different crops and agricultural practices.
questions.hint: Agro-climatic zones are defined by climate, soil, and water resources.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding India's food grain production trends: I. India has achieved self-sufficiency in food grain production since the Green Revolution. II. The per capita availability of pulses has consistently increased over the last two decades. III. Climatic variability and extreme weather events pose significant challenges to future food grain security. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.explanation: Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II is incorrect.
Both statements I and III are correct.
Statement II is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: India has largely achieved self-sufficiency in food grain production post-Green Revolution, moving from a deficit to a surplus nation. Statement III is correct: Climate change, leading to erratic monsoons, droughts, and floods, significantly threatens India's food grain security. Statement II is incorrect: Despite overall increases in pulse production, per capita availability of pulses has shown fluctuations and, at times, a decline due to population growth and consumption patterns, remaining a concern for nutritional security.
questions.hint: Analyze each statement carefully, considering trends in food grain production and consumption.
questions.subject: dsssb-gk

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily a Kharif crop in India?

options.explanation: Wheat is a Rabi crop.
Barley is a Rabi crop.
Rice is the most prominent Kharif crop.
Gram is a Rabi crop.

questions.explanation: Kharif crops are monsoon crops, sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October). Rice is the most prominent Kharif crop. Wheat, Barley, and Gram are Rabi crops.
questions.hint: Kharif crops are grown during the monsoon season.

questions.question: Which Indian state is the largest producer of Bauxite, a primary ore for aluminium?

options.explanation: Jharkhand is a major mineral producer but not the largest for bauxite.
Odisha is the largest producer of bauxite in India.
Madhya Pradesh is not the largest producer of bauxite.
Gujarat is not the largest producer of bauxite.

questions.explanation: Odisha possesses the largest bauxite reserves in India and is also the largest producer of bauxite, accounting for over half of India's total production.
questions.hint: Consider the major mineral-producing states in India.

questions.question: The 'Green Revolution' in India primarily focused on increasing the production of which two crops?

options.explanation: Cotton and Jute were not the primary focus of the Green Revolution.
Pulses and Oilseeds were not the primary focus of the Green Revolution.
Wheat and Rice were the primary focus of the Green Revolution.
Sugarcane and Tea were not the primary focus of the Green Revolution.

questions.explanation: The Green Revolution, initiated in the mid-1960s, largely concentrated on improving the yields of staple food grains, particularly wheat and rice, through the introduction of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.
questions.hint: The Green Revolution aimed to boost food grain production.

questions.question: Match the following agricultural schemes with their primary objectives: 1. PM-KISAN, 2. PM Fasal Bima Yojana, 3. Soil Health Card Scheme

Incorrect pairing of schemes and objectives.
Correct pairing: PM-KISAN (P), PM Fasal Bima Yojana (R), Soil Health Card Scheme (Q).
Incorrect pairing of schemes and objectives.

questions.explanation: PM-KISAN provides financial support to farmers, PM Fasal Bima Yojana offers crop insurance, and Soil Health Card Scheme assesses soil nutrient status.
questions.hint: Match each scheme with its core function.

questions.question: What is 'Drip Irrigation' primarily designed to achieve?

options.explanation: Drip irrigation reduces water evaporation.

options.text: Deliver water directly to the root zone of plants
options.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone.

options.text: Flood entire fields for uniform watering
options.explanation: Drip irrigation does not flood entire fields.

options.text: Promote growth of weeds in dry areas
options.explanation: Drip irrigation does not promote weed growth.

questions.explanation: Drip irrigation is a micro-irrigation system that saves water and fertilizer by allowing water to drip slowly to the roots of plants, either from above the soil surface or buried below the surface.
questions.hint: Drip irrigation is a water-saving technique.

questions.question: In which type of forest are trees like Sal, Teak, and Sandalwood predominantly found in India?

options.explanation: Tropical Evergreen Forests do not predominantly feature Sal, Teak, or Sandalwood.
Sal, Teak, and Sandalwood are characteristic of Tropical Deciduous Forests.
Montane Forests do not predominantly feature Sal, Teak, or Sandalwood.
Mangrove Forests do not predominantly feature Sal, Teak, or Sandalwood.

questions.explanation: Tropical Deciduous Forests, also known as Monsoon Forests, are the most widespread forests in India. Trees like Sal, Teak, and Sandalwood are characteristic species of these forests.
questions.hint: Consider the type of forests where these trees naturally grow.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Minimum Support Price (MSP) in India is INCORRECT?

options.text: It is announced by the government for certain crops before the sowing season.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: It aims to protect farmers from excessive fall in prices during bumper production.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: It is legally binding for all private traders to purchase crops at or above MSP.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect; MSP is not legally binding for private traders.

options.text: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) recommends MSPs.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

questions.explanation: While MSP is a crucial policy tool, it is not legally binding for private traders to purchase crops at or above the MSP. It primarily serves as a benchmark and a guarantee for public procurement.
questions.hint: MSP is a policy tool but not legally enforceable for private traders.

questions.question: Which of the following states is known for having the highest installed wind power capacity in India?

options.explanation: Gujarat is a significant contributor to wind power but not the highest.
Rajasthan has wind power capacity but not the highest in India.
Correct. Tamil Nadu leads in installed wind power capacity.
Maharashtra has wind power capacity but not the highest.

questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has historically been and continues to be the leading state in India in terms of installed wind power generation capacity, owing to its favourable coastal geography and consistent wind patterns.
questions.hint: This state is located in southern India and is known for its coastal regions.

questions.question: The concept of 'Biosphere Reserves' is primarily aimed at:

options.explanation: Tourism is not the primary aim of Biosphere Reserves.

options.text: Conserving biodiversity and promoting sustainable use of natural resources
options.explanation: Correct. This is the primary aim of Biosphere Reserves.
Breeding endangered species is not the sole purpose.
Commercial plantations are not the focus of Biosphere Reserves.

questions.explanation: Biosphere Reserves are areas designated by UNESCO to reconcile the conservation of biodiversity and the sustainable use of natural resources. They aim to achieve three main functions: conservation, development, and logistic support.
questions.hint: Think about the balance between conservation and human use.

questions.question: The 'Black Soil' (Regur soil) in India is particularly well-suited for the cultivation of which crop?

options.explanation: Tea is typically grown in hilly regions, not black soil.
Wheat is grown in other soil types, not primarily black soil.
Correct. Black soil is ideal for cotton cultivation.
Jute is grown in alluvial soil, not black soil.

questions.explanation: Black soil, also known as Regur soil, is highly fertile and has excellent moisture-retention capacity. These characteristics make it ideal for the cultivation of cotton, hence it is often referred to as 'black cotton soil'.
questions.hint: This crop is widely grown in the Deccan Plateau region.

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily a Kharif crop in India?

options.explanation: Wheat is a Rabi crop, sown in winter and harvested in spring.
Barley is a Rabi crop, grown in winter.
Gram (chickpea) is a Rabi crop, sown in winter.
Rice is the most important Kharif crop in India, sown during the monsoon season.

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India, initiated in the mid-1960s, primarily aimed at increasing the production of which crops?

options.explanation: Pulses and oilseeds were not the primary focus of the Green Revolution.
Wheat and rice were the main crops targeted by the Green Revolution.
Fruits and vegetables were not the focus of the Green Revolution.
Sugarcane and cotton were not the primary crops of the Green Revolution.

questions.explanation: The Green Revolution focused on the introduction of High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of seeds, especially for wheat and rice, along with improved irrigation facilities and chemical fertilizers, to boost food grain production.
questions.hint: The Green Revolution targeted staple food crops to address food security.

questions.question: Match the following agricultural practices with their descriptions: I. Jhum Cultivation, II. Terrace Farming, III. Sericulture, IV. Mixed Farming

options.explanation: Incorrect pairing of practices and descriptions.
Correct pairing: Jhum Cultivation (Q), Terrace Farming (R), Sericulture (P), Mixed Farming (S).
Incorrect pairing of practices and descriptions.
Incorrect pairing of practices and descriptions.

questions.explanation: Jhum cultivation is a form of shifting cultivation. Terrace farming is practiced on slopes to prevent soil erosion. Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms for silk. Mixed farming involves both crop cultivation and animal husbandry.
questions.hint: Jhum cultivation is associated with North-Eastern India, and sericulture involves silk production.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian states is the largest producer of crude Mica?

options.explanation: Jharkhand was historically a major producer but is no longer the largest.
Andhra Pradesh is currently the largest producer of crude mica in India.
Rajasthan is a producer but not the largest.
Bihar is not a major producer of mica.

questions.explanation: While Jharkhand (Koderma) is historically known for its mica belt, Andhra Pradesh (particularly the Nellore district) is currently the largest producer of crude mica in India.
questions.hint: Andhra Pradesh is a major producer of mica in India.

questions.question: The 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana' (PMFBY) scheme, launched in 2016, primarily provides:

options.text: Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 22 mandated crops.
options.explanation: MSP is provided under a different scheme, not PMFBY.

options.text: Direct income support to small and marginal farmers.
options.explanation: Direct income support is provided under schemes like PM-KISAN, not PMFBY.

options.text: Comprehensive crop insurance against non-preventable natural risks.
options.explanation: PMFBY provides crop insurance against natural calamities, pests, and diseases.

options.text: Subsidies for agricultural machinery and farm implements.
options.explanation: Subsidies for machinery are provided under different schemes, not PMFBY.

questions.explanation: PMFBY is a flagship crop insurance scheme aimed at providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen events like natural calamities, pests, and diseases.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest cotton-producing state in India?

options.explanation: Maharashtra is a significant cotton producer but not the largest.
Gujarat is the largest cotton-producing state in India.
Telangana is a notable cotton producer but ranks below Gujarat.
Punjab is not a major cotton-producing state in India.

questions.explanation: Gujarat is the largest cotton-producing state in India, contributing over 30% of the country's total cotton production. Maharashtra and Telangana are also significant producers but rank below Gujarat.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Green Revolution in India is/are correct?

i. It was launched in the mid-1960s.
ii. It primarily focused on increasing the production of rice and wheat.
iii. It led to a significant decline in the use of chemical fertilizers.

options.explanation: Statement i is correct, but statements ii and iii are also relevant.
Statements i and ii are correct, while statement iii is incorrect.
Statement iii is incorrect as the Green Revolution increased chemical fertilizer use.
Statement iii is incorrect, and statement i is also correct.

questions.explanation: The Green Revolution in India was launched in the mid-1960s to boost agricultural productivity, especially for rice and wheat. However, it also led to an increased use of chemical fertilizers, contradicting statement iii. Thus, only statements i and ii are correct.

questions.question: The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aims to address climate change issues in agriculture. Which of the following is NOT a component of NMSA?

options.explanation: Rainfed Area Development is a component of NMSA.
Soil Health Management is a component of NMSA.
PMFBY is not a component of NMSA; it is a separate crop insurance scheme.
National Mission on Micro Irrigation is a component of NMSA.

questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a separate scheme aimed at providing crop insurance to farmers and is not a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA). The other options are components of NMSA.
questions.hint: Review the components of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture.

questions.question: If a farmer wants to adopt precision farming techniques in India, which of the following technologies would be most directly useful for soil health monitoring?

options.explanation: Drones are useful for crop spraying but not specifically for soil health monitoring.
GPS-enabled tractors aid in precision farming but are not directly used for soil health monitoring.

options.text: Remote sensing and GIS for soil mapping
options.explanation: Remote sensing and GIS are directly useful for mapping soil health parameters.
IoT-based weather stations provide weather data but are not primarily used for soil health monitoring.

questions.explanation: Remote sensing and GIS (Geographic Information System) are most directly useful for soil health monitoring as they help in mapping soil variability, nutrient levels, and moisture content, enabling precision farming. While other technologies like drones and IoT-based systems are useful, they are not as directly related to soil health monitoring.
questions.hint: Consider technologies that provide detailed soil data for precision farming.

questions.question: The minimum support price (MSP) for a crop is announced by the Government of India to ensure remunerative prices to farmers. Which of the following crops is NOT covered under the MSP scheme as of 2023?

options.explanation: Wheat is covered under the MSP scheme.
Cotton is covered under the MSP scheme.
Sugarcane is covered under a different pricing mechanism but still under government support.
Potato is not covered under the MSP scheme as of 2023.

questions.explanation: As of 2023, the MSP scheme covers 23 crops, including wheat, cotton, and sugarcane, but potato is not included in this list. Sugarcane is covered under a different pricing mechanism (Fair and Remunerative Price), but it still falls under government price support schemes.
questions.hint: Check the list of crops covered under the MSP scheme.
